column1: # Golden precedence reference for hooks/reasons.tsv, maintained INDEPENDENTLY of
# that file. tests/cases/data-reasons.sh used to compare reasons.tsv's row order
# against the precedence comment at the top of reasons.tsv itself, which is
# self-consistency: one hand edits both, and a swap made in both places passes.
# The order is not arbitrary and this file states WHY, in bands, so a future edit
# has to argue against the reasoning rather than just move a line:
#   measurement   Could the hook read anything at all? If not, nothing below it
#                 was evaluated against real state, so nothing below it may deny.
#   identity      WHO is dispatching. A nested or forked call is refused whatever
#                 else is right about it, because the dispatcher is the thing that
#                 is wrong.
#   addressing    WHICH row and role the dispatch names. Until the tag resolves to
#                 a row, no cell of the table can be read, so every table rule
#                 below is unanswerable.
#   routing       The model: named at all, then high enough. Missing outranks too-low
#                 because a dispatch with no model has not made the choice yet.
#   applicability Is this phase part of THIS wave (scope, condition), and is it
#                 allowed to run YET (order)? A phase that is not in the wave is a
#                 mistake worth naming before one that is merely early.
#   evidence      The hand-off artifacts and the approvals that gate a re-run.
#   spending      Rounds, pasted context, budget: real but recoverable overruns.
#   session       The orchestrator-only rules, one per tool surface.
#   commit        What may reach a commit.
#   stop          What a subagent may return.
#   advisory      Warn-only. Nothing here ever denies, so nothing here can outrank
#                 a rule that does.
precedence
